source: can you make a game where your a cat and you have to scratch furniture to get money and with the money you can buy different cat patterns that makes you stronger and the map is a massive house and you are very small and it makes your avatar look like a cat

answers.ask: What kind of house - a cosy modern family home, something grand and old, or stylized and cartoon?
answers.answer: Use a cosy modern family home, built with a playful cartoon style.

answers.ask: How small is the cat relative to the furniture? That decides whether a normal house needs to be built at two or three times normal size.
answers.answer: Make the cat very small relative to the furniture, with the house built at roughly three times normal scale so furniture feels huge.

answers.ask: Is there an end to the loop - all patterns unlocked, all furniture destroyed - or does it just keep going?
answers.answer: The game keeps going as an ongoing scratch-and-upgrade loop; the prompt does not call for a final ending.

## Clarifications resolved
- [author] theme — Q: What kind of house - a cosy modern family home, something grand and old, or stylized and cartoon? A: Use a cosy modern family home, built with a playful cartoon style.
- [author] scale — Q: How small is the cat relative to the furniture? That decides whether a normal house needs to be built at two or three times normal size. A: Make the cat very small relative to the furniture, with the house built at roughly three times normal scale so furniture feels huge.
- [author] goal — Q: Is there an end to the loop - all patterns unlocked, all furniture destroyed - or does it just keep going? A: The game keeps going as an ongoing scratch-and-upgrade loop; the prompt does not call for a final ending.
- [agent_inferred] verticality — Q: Does the playable house require multiple floors? A: No; use one oversized ground-floor interior so all furniture remains visible and reachable in one frame.

## Enriched image prompt
Build the interior of a cosy modern family home in a playful cartoon style, scaled to roughly three times normal size so a very small cat avatar feels tiny beside every object. Use one continuous oversized ground floor with an open living room, dining area, kitchen edge, and short connecting hall. Fill it with clearly separated scratchable furniture clusters: a huge sofa and armchairs, dining chairs, table legs, rugs, cabinets, and other ordinary household pieces, while leaving cat-width routes around and beneath them. Emphasize the towering furniture scale from a readable isometric view and keep the entire playable interior enclosed, with no exterior or upper floor.

## Genre
The dominant genre is Simulation because the repeated scratch-and-upgrade loop drives play.

## Shape and preset
Use `interior-single`, a Zone (Single Interior), taken from outside Simulation’s usual shape list because the massive house interior is the entire map. The closest preset is Incremental Simulator, but after replacing its world shape and dropping its unrequested shop and gate geometry it is no longer recognizable, so the preset is none.

## Config requirements
Use the visible side of `trigger-task` for the oversized sofas, chairs, table legs, rugs, and cabinets that act as repeated scratching stations. Cat patterns, strength, money, purchasing, and avatar morphing are mechanics rather than map geometry.

## Layout requirements
Place `trigger-task` as TriggerZone surfaces on each major scratchable furniture cluster, aligned to reachable lower edges at cat height. Distribute them across the living, dining, and kitchen-adjacent spaces so the ongoing loop circulates through the full house.

## Layout components
The map is one enclosed, single-level house interior at three times normal scale. Its zones are an open living room, dining area, kitchen edge, and short hall, connected without loading transitions. Oversized furniture creates the principal props and landmarks, with clear miniature-cat circulation around and beneath pieces. Outer walls enclose the frame; no exterior or upstairs is built.

## Render order
Use `isometric`: render the exaggerated cartoon interior first because the scale relationship and visual composition lead, then derive the straightforward top-down plan.

## Scale, theme, and pipeline cost
The scale band is medium because one oversized house must fit while individual furniture stations remain legible. The theme is a cosy modern family home in playful cartoon styling. The pipeline cost is `P0`: one interior-only surface has no outside transition, overhang route, or required procedural topology.
